definitions.explanation: The act of committing a crime, or a crime that has been committed. A formal legal and literary term used in judicial and historical contexts.

examples.japanese: {罪犯|ざいはん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{証拠|しょうこ}→証拠：10575_shouko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{裁判|さいばん}→裁判：02773_saiban⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{示|しめ}された→示す：01948_shimesu⟧。
examples.english: Evidence of the criminal act was presented at the trial.

examples.japanese: ⟦{過去|かこ}→過去：00152_kako⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{罪犯|ざいはん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{悔|く}い{改|あらた}め→悔い改める：19907_kuiaratameru⟧、⟦{社会|しゃかい}{復帰|ふっき}→社会復帰：20417_shakaifukki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{目指|めざ}す→目指す：10528_mezasu⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{少|すく}なくない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧。
examples.english: There are quite a few people who repent of their past offenses and aim to reintegrate into society.

notes:
Composed of {罪|ざい} (crime, sin, guilt) and {犯|はん} (offense, perpetration). A formal term found in legal documents, historical texts, and literary writing. In everyday language, ⟦{犯罪|はんざい}→犯罪：03569_hanzai⟧ (crime) is the standard term; {罪犯|ざいはん} reverses the character order and carries a more literary or archaic tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罪犯|ざいはん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{犯|おか}す→犯す：10059_okasu⟧: to commit an offense
- {罪犯|ざいはん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{記録|きろく}→記録：02490_kiroku⟧: record of criminal acts
- {重|じゅう}{罪犯|ざいはん}: serious offense

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{犯罪|はんざい}→犯罪：03569_hanzai⟧: crime — the standard, everyday term with reversed character order
- ⟦{罪|つみ}→罪：03532_tsumi⟧: sin, crime, guilt — can be used in both legal and moral senses
- ⟦{犯行|はんこう}→犯行：13472_hankou⟧: criminal act — emphasizes the specific action of committing a crime
